title: Review of c07's ringswim-256 (SIMD): swimming and a bounded, band-free population replicate on seed 43, but all 3 random 'divisions' are re-separations of cells that had just collided (46% of qualifying splits)
summary: Fresh seed 43 at 256^2, T=20000: walled cells form from noise and stay a bounded population of ~35-45 crescents and round cells with no domain-wrapping band (sheet.png). The author's celltrack gives 144 persistent splits, max generation 15, splits/merges 353/237, 100 track segments >= 3 BL (best 10.5 BL); labkit counts 771 splits, 647 merges and 0 persistent splits at its K=2000 window. Strips of 3 randomly drawn late binary splits (both children living >= 1000 t; strip_s43.png) all show two cells that had touched pulling apart, and in each case the parent track was a merge product of the previous 100-280 t. Over all binary splits whose children live >= 400 t, 44/96 (46%) follow a merge within 600 t (merge_then_split.py), so the persistent-split count and the generation depth are inflated by collision re-separations; the remaining ~52 are candidates for genuine pinching that I did not inspect.

observations.S: rerun/seed43/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain; cells by t=800
observations.I: rerun/seed43/sheet.png: a bounded population of walled cells of similar size to t=20000, no band
observations.M: data/celltrack_s43.log: 100 segments >= 3 BL, 19 >= 5 BL, best 10.5 BL; crescents with depletion wakes in sheet.png

seeds_run.result: S, I, M pass; D counts inflated by re-separations

not_checked: D on the ~52 splits not preceded by a merge (not inspected)
verdicts.limitation: Division is not established on this seed: all three randomly drawn splits are cells separating after a collision (strip_s43.png rows 627, 696, 631; merge 100-280 t earlier), 46% of qualifying splits follow a merge within 600 t, and labkit finds 0 persistent splits. celltrack's generation depth (15) counts these re-separations. A split count that excludes merge products of the last ~600 t, and strips drawn from that set, are needed before D. The drive is a per-body averaged gradient.
